_comment: Persona C — Scope Navigator. 5-step design token rename with mixed explicit and inferred scope. Steps 1, 2, 4 carry targetFiles (no scope prompt expected). Steps 3, 5 have no targetFiles (scope prompt expected). Adapt to your repo.
name: persona-c-theme-update

tasks.label: Update token definition
tasks.input: in src/tokens/colors.ts rename the token 'primary-500' to 'brand-600' — update both the key name and any comments that reference it
tasks._note: Explicit targetFiles. Expect no scope prompt.

tasks.label: Update Button component class
tasks.input: in src/components/Button.tsx replace any className string or Tailwind class that references 'primary-500' with 'brand-600'
tasks._note: Explicit targetFiles. Expect no scope prompt.

tasks.label: Update Tailwind config
tasks.input: in the Tailwind config file add a 'brand' color scale that maps brand-600 to the hex value previously used for primary-500 — the config file is typically tailwind.config.js or tailwind.config.ts at the project root
tasks._note: No targetFiles. Expect scope prompt with candidates. Observation: is the config file findable in the candidate list? Does the reviewer select it confidently?

tasks.label: Update Storybook stories
tasks.input: in the Storybook story files for Button and Badge replace all occurrences of 'primary-500' with 'brand-600' in className strings and documentation strings
tasks._note: Multiple explicit targetFiles. Expect no scope prompt. Observation: does multi-file targetFiles feel natural?

tasks.label: Update global CSS variables
tasks.input: in the global CSS file replace the CSS custom property '--color-primary-500' with '--color-brand-600' and update its value if needed
tasks._note: No targetFiles. Global CSS could be src/index.css, src/styles/global.css, or similar. Expect scope prompt. Observation: is the candidate list helpful when the file name is ambiguous?
